title: Terraform stability curation and provider deprecation timeline
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We lack a single curated timeline and scoring system that guides when Terraform providers and internal modules can be upgraded in Private (VPC) deployments. Current practice is ad-hoc: module owners pin to arbitrary provider versions which causes drift, long-lived forks, and surprise breakages during infra upgrades.

Goal: Deliver a reproducible compatibility curation process and an automated deprecation timeline for Terraform providers and first-party modules used in Private deployments. Outputs: (1) compatibility matrix CSV + human-facing view, (2) provider stability score and deprecation timeline, (3) automated PR generator in infra repo that proposes pin bumps with test results, (4) CI smoke harness for post-upgrade health checks, (5) runbook for staged rollout and rollback.

Scope: AWS, GCP, and Azure providers and top-level modules (vpc, eks, rds, vault, k8s-addons, network-inspector) used by Private customers. Excludes community modules not curated by Platform team.

Non-goal: Rewriting modules or performing full migrations in this ticket. Those will be separate follow-ups triggered by the matrix findings.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix generated for current production module/provider combos and committed to infra/docs/provider-compat.csv
Automated PR bot (infra/auto-pin-bot) can open a proposed pin bump for a provider with associated CI results
Stability scoring logic documented and agreed by Platform leads (stability score >= 0-100) and used to assign deprecation week windows
CI smoke harness implements 5 post-upgrade probes (control-plane readiness, KV cache warm, auth flows, private networking e2e, sample inference call) and runs on auto-PRs
Runbook with staged rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%) and automated rollback hooks published in Confluence and linked from the PR template
implementation_notes: Define a 3-factor stability score: semantic-compat (API/major/minor changes), community-adoption (downloads/major releases), infra-compat (known provider bug regressions). Score is 0-100; >=75 is green, 50-75 is guarded, <50 requires manual sign-off.

Automation: infra/auto-pin-bot will use the matrix + upstream provider release feed to generate candidate bumps. Each candidate opens a branch and CI runs the smoke harness. PR body includes stability score and links to test artifacts.

Smoke harness: runs in ephemeral canary workspace using sample terraform workspace with trimmed module set (vpc + minimal eks). Must provide deterministic teardown and health-check artifacts (cloudwatch logs snapshots, endpoints, k8s pod statuses).

Rollout policy: canary in a dedicated staging account -> 24h observation window -> 25% production accounts via blue/green policy -> 100% after automated health gates. If any gate fails, roll back to previous provider pin and open incident ticket.

Pinning policy: default pins at minor version (e.g., 5.32.x) for providers with stability >=75; caret-style allowed in private manifests only after 90+ stability and explicit review. Record pins in provider-constraints.tf and lockfiles in the infra repo.
Communication: publish weekly update on matrix changes to #platform-iac and notify affected product owners when stability drops below 60 for a provider used by their customers.
risks_and_tradeoffs: Conservative pinning reduces surprise breakages but increases maintenance overhead for backports and security fixes.
Automated PRs reduce manual effort but can create noise; throttling and grouping rules will be necessary (group minor bumps weekly, major bumps manually).
Running smoke harness in ephemeral workspaces increases CI cost; we will cap full e2e runs to candidate PRs where stability<80 or module touches critical infra (VPC/EKS).
work_plan: Week 1 (current): draft stability scoring rubric, inventory modules/providers, implement compatibility CSV generator script (infra/tools/compat-scan)
Week 2: implement smoke harness and CI job, wire automated PR generator (auto-pin-bot) to infra repo, land initial matrix CSV in docs/
Week 3: run a controlled canary upgrade for aws provider minor bump in staging account, validate rollback path, capture runbook steps
Week 4: roll to 25% production, monitor metrics (token success rate, request latency, infra errors), finalize runbook and on-call instructions
